title: Pay, ask for a waiver of, or appeal a parking ticket
question: I got a parking ticket in Staunton. How do I pay it, and how do I contest it?
summary: Staunton parking tickets are paid to the City Treasurer in person at City Hall, in a parking-ticket drop box, or by mail, not online. Pay within 10 days of the ticket date. After that a $10 late fee is added and a final notice gives 10 business days more; then a court summons is issued and only the General District Court takes payment. To contest, file the Police Department's review form with the ticket. The Commonwealth's Attorney decides, and payment is on hold meanwhile. If the ticket is not dismissed, pay within 15 days of the letter. State law sends any contest to the General District Court, and a conviction there can be appealed to circuit court within 10 days.

legal_basis.quote: The governing body of any county, city, or town may by ordinance provide for the regulation of parking, stopping, and standing of vehicles within its limits

The ordinance may delegate to that department, official, or employee the authority to make and enforce any additional regulations concerning parking that may be required, including penalties for violations, deadlines for the payment of fines, and late payment penalties for fines not paid when due.

Such ordinance may also provide that a summons or parking ticket for the violation of the ordinance or regulations may be issued by law-enforcement officers, other uniformed employees of the locality, or by uniformed personnel serving under contract with the locality.
shall constitute in evidence a prima facie presumption that the registered owner of the vehicle was the person who committed the violation
That uncontested payment of parking citation penalties be collected and accounted for by a local administrative official or officials
That contest by any person of any parking citation shall be certified on an appropriate form, to the appropriate district court, by such official or officials
That the local administrative official or officials shall cause complaints, summons, or warrants to be issued for delinquent parking citations.

Every action to collect unpaid parking citation penalties imposed for violation of a city or county ordinance regulating parking under this article shall be commenced within three years of the date upon which such penalty became delinquent.
Unless otherwise stated, these violations shall constitute traffic infractions punishable by a fine of not more than that provided for a Class 4 misdemeanor under § 18.2-11 .
Any local governing body, by such ordinance, may assess and retain a fine of not less than $100 nor more than $500 for its violation.
An appearance may be made in person or in writing by mail to a clerk of court or in person before a magistrate, prior to any date fixed for trial in court.

Fines imposed under local traffic infraction ordinances that do not parallel provisions of state law and fulfill the criteria set out in subsection A may be prepayable in the manner set forth in subsection B if such ordinances appear in a schedule entered by order of the local circuit courts.
In traffic infractions tried in district court, there shall be assessed as court costs a fixed fee of $51.
a fee of $35 shall be taxed as costs whenever a defendant fails to appear, unless, after a hearing requested by such person, good cause is shown for such failure to appear.

Any person convicted in a district court of an offense not felonious shall have the right, at any time within ten days from such conviction, and whether or not such conviction was upon a plea of guilty, to appeal to the circuit court.
Any appeal taken under the provisions of this chapter shall be heard de novo in the appellate court and shall be tried without formal pleadings in writing
he shall be deemed to have waived court hearing and the case may be heard in his absence, after which he shall be notified of the court's finding
For any traffic infraction case appealed to a circuit court, the defendant shall have the right to trial by jury.
Such designated infractions shall include violations of §§ 46.2-830.1 , 46.2-878.2 and 46.2-1242 or any parallel local ordinances.
The court shall offer any defendant the opportunity to enter into a deferred payment agreement, modified deferred payment agreement, or installment payment agreement.
any motor vehicle, vehicle, or trailer parked on the public highways or public grounds against which there are three or more unpaid or otherwise unsettled parking violation notices may be removed

by payment of the outstanding parking violation notices for which the motor vehicle, vehicle, or trailer was removed or immobilized and by payment of all costs incidental to the immobilization, removal, and storage of the motor vehicle, vehicle, or trailer

whereby the Commissioner will refuse to issue or renew any vehicle registration of any applicant therefor who owes to such county, city, or town any local vehicle license fees or delinquent tangible personal property tax or parking citations.

shall provide the debtor notice of the intent to deny renewal of registration or issuance of registration for any currently unregistered vehicle at least 30 days prior to the expiration date of a current vehicle registration

In the case of parking violations, the Commissioner shall only refuse to issue or renew the vehicle registration of any applicant therefor pursuant to this subsection for the vehicle that incurred the parking violations.

steps.step: Read the ticket and note its date: the 10-day payment clock starts on the date of the ticket
steps.who: Person who received the ticket (by state law the vehicle's registered owner is presumed responsible)
steps.how: This process covers tickets written by the City of Staunton. Note the ticket number, the date, the violation and the City Code section printed on it. Decide early whether to pay or contest: the lower amount applies only within 10 days.
steps.deadline: Pay within 10 days from the date of the ticket
steps.quote: Parking tickets must be paid within 10 days from the date of the ticket.

steps.step: Look up the fine on the City's parking fine schedule
steps.how: The Parking Tickets page links two PDFs. The current one, 'Parking Fines (effective Nov. 1, 2024)', is the City Manager's July 1, 2016 schedule with Executive Action No. 2024-08 in front of it, which adds a $50.00 fine for City Code § 10.25.100. Find your violation by City Code section (see fees). Most fines are $10.00 to $25.00. Disability spaces and trucks or motor homes in residential areas are $100.00. Overstaying a time limit on city streets or in city facilities is $50.00 for a first violation in 12 months and $150.00 after that.
steps.fee: $1.00 to $150.00 depending on the violation (see fees)
steps.quote: Effective July 1, 2016, and pursuant to my authority under § 10.05.090 and Chapter 10.25 of Title 10 of the Staunton City Code, I promulgate the following schedule of fines for violations of parking restrictions applicable in the City of Staunton.

steps.step: Pay in person at the Treasurer's Office
steps.who: Person who received the ticket, paying the City Treasurer
steps.how: Go to the Treasurer's Office: City Hall, 1st floor (Beverley Street entrance), 116 W. Beverley Street. It is open 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday. Bring the ticket. The pages do not say which payment methods the office takes for parking tickets.
steps.deadline: Within 10 days from the date of the ticket
steps.quote: You can pay a parking ticket at the Treasurer’s Office in City Hall, or drop off your payment in a parking ticket drop box.

steps.step: Or leave the payment in a parking ticket drop box
steps.who: Person who received the ticket, paying the City Treasurer
steps.how: Drop boxes are on N. Augusta St. behind First Bank, on Frederick Street in front of Mary Baldwin University, in the Augusta Street Parking Lot, and on Central Avenue near W. Beverley Street. The Treasurer's payment page says the green drop box on Central Avenue under the clock tower takes all city payments, by check or money order only, 24 hours a day. Do not put cash in a drop box.
steps.deadline: Within 10 days from the date of the ticket
steps.quote: Drop box locations include N. Augusta St. behind First Bank; Frederick Street in front of Mary Baldwin University; the Augusta Street Parking Lot and on Central Avenue near the intersection of W. Beverley Street.

steps.step: Or pay by mail (parking tickets cannot be paid online)
steps.who: Person who received the ticket, paying the City Treasurer
steps.how: Mail the payment to City of Staunton, PO Box 474, Staunton, VA 24402-0474, the address the Treasurer's payment page gives for all payments except utility bills. Allow time for mail delivery within the 10 days; the pages do not say whether the postmark or the date the City receives the payment counts. The City's online and phone payment services take only real estate tax, personal property tax and utility bills.
steps.deadline: Within 10 days from the date of the ticket
steps.quote: Parking tickets cannot be paid online but can be mailed, paid in person or paid via City drop box.

steps.step: If the ticket is not paid within 10 days, a $10 late fee is added and a final notice is mailed
steps.who: City Treasurer (collection); the ticket holder pays
steps.how: Pay the ticket plus the $10 late fee by any method in s3 to s5 within 10 business days from the date of the final notice letter.
steps.deadline: 10 business days from the date of the final notice letter
steps.fee: The fine plus a $10 late fee (administration fee)
steps.quote: After 10 days have passed, a $10 late fee (administration fee) is added to the cost of the ticket and a final notice will be sent.

steps.step: If the final notice is not paid, a Virginia Uniform Summons is issued to appear in court
steps.who: City (causes the summons to be issued, as state law requires for delinquent tickets); Staunton General District Court
steps.how: From then on the Treasurer's Office no longer accepts payment for the ticket. The summons gives the court date.
steps.deadline: Issued if the ticket is not paid within 10 business days of the final notice
steps.quote: If the ticket has not been paid after 10 business days, a Virginia Uniform Summons will be issued for you to appear in court.

steps.step: After a summons: prepay at the General District Court Clerk's Office before the court date, or go to court
steps.who: Person summoned (defendant); Staunton General District Court Clerk's Office
steps.how: Pay at the Clerk's Office, 113 E. Beverley St., 1st Floor (8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; (540) 332-3878), or by mail to the court named on the summons. Prepaying counts as giving up the hearing and pleading guilty. A mailed prepayment counts only when the court receives it, not on the date it is mailed. If the case shows 'Mark for Payment' in the court's online case system, it can also be paid online by card, with a 4% convenience fee. Online payments must be made before 3:30 p.m. on the business day before the trial date.
steps.deadline: Before the court date on the summons (online: before 3:30 p.m. on the business day before the trial date; mail: at least 7 days before the court date is advised)
steps.fee: The fine plus court costs; state law sets a $51 fixed fee for traffic infractions (the amount the Staunton court charges for a parking case was not found)
steps.quote: Once a summons has been issued, the Treasurer’s Office will no longer accept payment.

steps.step: To contest the ticket, fill out the Police Department's review form and hand it in with the ticket
steps.how: Use the form 'Request for Administrative Review of Parking Citation' (f1). Fill in your name, address, the parking ticket number, the violation date, plate number, violation and location. Write why the ticket should be dismissed, then sign and date it to certify that your statement is true. Attach the parking ticket. Return it to the Records Division of the Staunton Police Department, City Hall basement floor, 116 W. Beverley St. (the department's business hours are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday; its page gives 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. for in-person crash-report requests, so arriving before 4 p.m. is the safer choice). The form says it is for protesting a ticket without waiting for a criminal summons and trial. No filing deadline is stated, so filing within the 10 days for payment is the cautious choice.
steps.quote: You can fill out and submit a contest form at the Police Department.

steps.step: The Police Department sends the form to the Commonwealth's Attorney for review; payment is on hold meanwhile
steps.who: Staunton Police Department (adds the issuing officer's comments and forwards the form); Commonwealth's Attorney, City of Staunton (decides)
steps.how: You do not have to pay while the review is pending. The decision comes by mail. The pages give no time for the decision. If no letter comes, you can call the Parking Tickets line (540.332.3856) or the Police Department (540.332.3845) to ask about the form; the pages do not describe this follow-up.
steps.fee: Payment requirement on hold during review
steps.quote: While your request for dismissal is under review, the payment requirement is placed on hold until you receive correspondence from the Police Department about the status of your ticket.

steps.step: Read the decision letter: dismissed, or pay within 15 days
steps.who: Commonwealth's Attorney (decision); Police Department (sends the letter); the ticket holder
steps.how: The review section of the form has two outcomes: 'Considered Favorably. Charge dismissed, no fine due.' or 'Not Considered Favorably. Payment due of $' with an amount filled in. If the ticket is not dismissed, pay it within 15 days from the date of the letter. The page does not say where; the ways to pay a ticket that the City's pages give are the Treasurer's Office, the drop boxes and mail (s3 to s5), unless the letter says otherwise. See s12 if you want a judge to decide.
steps.deadline: 15 days from the date of the letter
steps.fee: The amount due stated on the decision (the form leaves the amount blank for the reviewer)
steps.quote: If the ticket is not dismissed you will have 15 days from the date of the letter to pay the ticket.

steps.step: If you still dispute the ticket, have it decided by the Staunton General District Court
steps.who: Ticket holder; the City (certifies the contest to the court); Staunton General District Court
steps.how: State law requires a city's parking ordinance to send any contest of a parking ticket to the district court. Staunton's pages do not say how to ask for this directly. Under § 46.2-1225 the local official who collects uncontested payments is the one who certifies a contest to the court, so a reasonable step (not one the City describes) is to ask the Treasurer's Office, or the Police Department, which handles contest forms, how to have the contest certified to court, before the 15 days run out. Otherwise, an unpaid ticket leads to a summons with a court date (s6, s7), and the $10 late fee may be added on the way. In court, proof that the vehicle was parked illegally and that you were its registered owner is prima facie evidence that you committed the violation (Va. Code § 46.2-1220).
steps.quote: That contest by any person of any parking citation shall be certified on an appropriate form, to the appropriate district court, by such official or officials

steps.step: Go to the hearing in the Staunton General District Court
steps.who: Defendant (registered owner); Staunton General District Court
steps.how: The court is at 113 E. Beverley St., 1st Floor. The court page lists traffic infractions at 9:30 a.m. and trials and contested cases at 10:30 a.m. on its traffic and criminal days (every Wednesday, the 5th Thursday, and the 1st, 3rd and 5th Fridays, holidays excepted); it does not mention parking cases. The date on your summons controls. The clerk grants a first continuance; later continuances need a judge's order on a motion. If, as Va. Code § 46.2-113 provides unless otherwise stated, the violation is a traffic infraction, a judge decides without a jury, and if you do not appear the case may be heard in your absence and you are notified of the finding (Va. Code § 19.2-258.1). If you are found guilty you pay the fine plus court costs. A $35 cost is added if you fail to appear, unless you ask for a hearing and show good cause.
steps.deadline: The court date on the summons
steps.fee: Fine plus a $51 fixed fee in traffic infractions if found guilty; $35 more if you fail to appear, unless good cause is shown at a hearing you request (Va. Code § 16.1-69.48:1)

steps.step: Appeal a General District Court conviction to the Staunton Circuit Court
steps.how: Note the appeal within 10 days of the conviction, even after a guilty plea (a prepayment is entered as a waiver of trial and a plea of guilty, Va. Code § 16.1-69.40:1(B)). The circuit court hears the case again from the start (de novo), and in a traffic infraction appeal the defendant has the right to a jury trial (Va. Code §§ 16.1-136, 19.2-258.1). Ask the General District Court Clerk's Office how to note the appeal and what it costs.
steps.deadline: Within ten days from the conviction
steps.quote: Any person convicted in a district court of an offense not felonious shall have the right, at any time within ten days from such conviction, and whether or not such conviction was upon a plea of guilty, to appeal to the circuit court.

steps.step: What can happen to tickets left unpaid
steps.who: City Treasurer; Staunton Police Department; Virginia DMV
steps.how: State law lets a treasurer agree with the DMV to refuse to issue or renew the registration of the vehicle that got the tickets; the agreement must give the debtor notice at least 30 days before the current registration expires. It also lets a city, by ordinance, tow or boot a vehicle parked on public highways or public grounds with three or more unpaid or unsettled tickets, which is released when the tickets and the towing, immobilization and storage costs are paid. Whether Staunton uses either was not found. The City must start any action to collect within three years of the date the penalty became delinquent.
steps.deadline: Collection must start within three years of delinquency (Va. Code § 46.2-1225)
steps.fee: Outstanding fines; any DMV enforcement fee and any towing, immobilization and storage costs (local amounts not found)
steps.quote: whereby the Commissioner will refuse to issue or renew any vehicle registration of any applicant therefor who owes to such county, city, or town any local vehicle license fees or delinquent tangible personal property tax or parking citations.

escalation.trigger: You think the ticket was wrong
escalation.next: Administrative review by the Commonwealth's Attorney, City of Staunton, through the Staunton Police Department (form f1)
escalation.deadline: None stated; payment is on hold while the review is pending
escalation.basis: City of Staunton Parking Tickets page (local procedure; no City Code section or state statute naming this review was found)
escalation.quote: The Police Department will process the contest form and send it to the Commonwealth’s Attorney for review.

escalation.trigger: No decision letter arrives after you file the contest form
escalation.next: Staunton Police Department (Parking Tickets line 540.332.3856 or 540.332.3845); payment stays on hold until the Police Department writes to you
escalation.basis: City of Staunton Parking Tickets page
escalation.quote: While your request for dismissal is under review, the payment requirement is placed on hold until you receive correspondence from the Police Department about the status of your ticket.

escalation.trigger: The Commonwealth's Attorney does not dismiss the ticket and you still dispute it
escalation.next: Staunton General District Court (trial of the contested ticket)
escalation.deadline: None found for asking; the city expects payment within 15 days of the letter, and an unpaid ticket leads to a late fee, a final notice and a summons
escalation.quote: That contest by any person of any parking citation shall be certified on an appropriate form, to the appropriate district court, by such official or officials

escalation.trigger: Convicted in the General District Court
escalation.next: Staunton Circuit Court (new trial, de novo)
escalation.deadline: Within ten days from the conviction
escalation.quote: Any person convicted in a district court of an offense not felonious shall have the right, at any time within ten days from such conviction, and whether or not such conviction was upon a plea of guilty, to appeal to the circuit court.

escalation.trigger: Found guilty in court and unable to pay the fine and costs at once
escalation.next: Staunton General District Court clerk: deferred or installment payment agreement (form DC-211, f2)
escalation.quote: The court shall offer any defendant the opportunity to enter into a deferred payment agreement, modified deferred payment agreement, or installment payment agreement.

escalation.trigger: The City tries to collect an old ticket more than three years after it became delinquent
escalation.next: Raise the time limit as a defence in the Staunton General District Court
escalation.deadline: Collection action must start within three years of delinquency
escalation.quote: Every action to collect unpaid parking citation penalties imposed for violation of a city or county ordinance regulating parking under this article shall be commenced within three years of the date upon which such penalty became delinquent.

caveats: The City of Staunton's website (www.ci.staunton.va.us) refuses automated readers, so the city pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The Parking Tickets page has the same text in its copies of 2026-09-01, 2026-05-07, 2026-01-16 and 2024-12-12. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them or by phone before you act.

Scanned documents. The fines PDF and the contest form are scans. Page 1 of the 2024 fines PDF (Executive Action No. 2024-08) has no text layer, and the other pages and the contest form carry a poor OCR layer ('Oty' for 'City', '$SO.DO'). The quotes from them are transcriptions from the page images, which a text search cannot confirm. The quotes keep the capitalisation as printed.

The two fine schedules. The Parking Tickets page and the Police Department page link 'Parking Fines (as of 2016)' (document 12620) and 'Parking Fines (effective Nov. 1, 2024)' (document 12622); the version numbers in both URLs decode to 2024-09-23 (an inference from the URL format). The 2024 file is Executive Action No. 2024-08 (signed 9/11/2024) followed by the City Manager's memorandum of May 25, 2016, effective July 1, 2016. The 2016 file is that memorandum alone. The only change found is the new $50.00 fine for City Code § 10.25.100. The memorandum and its copy list name City officials; no names are recorded here.

City Code § 10.25.100. Its subject was not read. A search engine's listing of the eCode360 table of contents suggests it is the time limit for parking inoperable vehicles; that is unverified. The Executive Action says only that the fine took effect November 1, 2024 'after the City complies with necessary notice provisions' of § 10.05.090.

City Code text. The Parking Tickets page links § 10.25.080 to the old Code Publishing site (codepublishing.com/VA/Staunton, Chapter 10.25), which refuses automated readers. The code is now on General Code's eCode360 (https://ecode360.com/ST4660), which also refuses automated readers and whose terms bar reproducing its content for public purposes. So no City Code text is quoted, and lexflow has not checked it. Section numbers and descriptions here come from the City Manager's fine schedule. No City Code source was found for the 10-day deadline, the $10 late fee, the final notice, the 15-day period or the Commonwealth's Attorney review; they come from the Parking Tickets page.

Late fee and meter rows. The schedule lists meter violations at $1.00 ('courtesy ticket'), $10.00 ('uncontested fine') and $10.00 ('fine with administrative charge') but does not say when each applies, or how the page's $10 late fee relates to them. When a $1.00 courtesy ticket is issued was not found.
Waiver. No first-ticket or one-time waiver programme (like Charlottesville's) was found for Staunton. The only route is the contest form, which asks for 'review and dismissal'.

Payment methods. The City pages do not say which methods the Treasurer's counter takes for parking tickets (cash, card or check), or whether the parking ticket drop boxes take anything besides check or money order. The check-or-money-order rule is stated for the green Central Avenue drop box under the clock tower. The mail address block on the Paying Taxes & Fees page includes the Treasurer's name, which is left out here. The pages do not say whether to write the ticket number on the check. The City's phone line (1.888.272.9829, jurisdiction code 1038) and online portal cover real estate tax, personal property tax and utility bills only.

Contest details. No deadline for filing a contest is stated, and the pages do not say whether a contest filed after the 10 days avoids the $10 late fee. The Parking Tickets page says to submit the form 'at the Police Department'; the form says to return it to the Records Division at 116 W. Beverley St. Mailing or emailing the form is not mentioned. The PoliceRecords mailbox is published for crash reports only. No processing time for the Commonwealth's Attorney's decision is stated. The form carries the printed code '5-29-84-78', whose meaning is unknown, and its URL stamp suggests it was posted on 2017-03-07.

Going to court. City sources do not say how a person whose contest is denied can ask for a court hearing without first letting the ticket go unpaid. Va. Code § 46.2-1225(2) requires the city's ordinance to certify any contest to the district court. Ask the Police Department or the Treasurer before the 15 days run out.

Court costs. No Staunton source states the court costs in a parking case. Va. Code § 46.2-113 makes violations of local ordinances adopted under Title 46.2 traffic infractions 'Unless otherwise stated', so the $51 fixed fee in Va. Code § 16.1-69.48:1(D) should apply on conviction or prepayment. That is an inference, and the City Code was not read. Local court assessments (City Code § 3.05.080, as summarised in curated/places/va/staunton/traffic_ticket.json) may be added; this was not confirmed for parking cases. Whether a city parking summons can be prepaid depends on Va. Code § 16.1-69.40:1 (a parallel state offence or a circuit court schedule under subsection D). The City page says you may prepay at the clerk's office, and online payment works only when the case shows 'Mark for Payment'.

Court schedule. The General District Court page lists traffic infractions at 9:30 a.m. on its traffic and criminal days but does not mention parking cases. The summons sets the date. The 25th District payment policy (https://www.vacourts.gov/static/online/ppp_fines_costs/dc/staunton.pdf) is described on the Staunton traffic ticket page.

Enforcement of unpaid tickets. Whether the Treasurer has a DMV registration-withholding agreement (Va. Code § 46.2-752(J)), or the City has a tow-or-boot ordinance for three or more unpaid tickets (Va. Code § 46.2-1216), was not found. The City's Parking page separately says vehicles left overnight on city property for more than seven consecutive days are subject to towing.

Scope. This covers tickets written under Staunton's City Code. Tickets on private lots (Va. Code § 46.2-1231), tickets from Augusta County, and any university or other institutional tickets are outside it and not covered here.

Privacy. The City pages name the Treasurer, the Commonwealth's Attorney and a deputy, and a FOIA contact with a personal mailbox. The court pages name the clerks and judges, and the fine schedule names City officials. None of these is recorded. Only office addresses, office lines, the role mailbox PoliceRecords@ci.staunton.va.us and official portals are listed.
Versions. Open US Law's copy of Va. Code § 46.2-1220 includes its 2026 amendments (2026, cc. 665, 938), and § 16.1-69.40:1 includes 2026, Sp. Sess. I, c. 1.

Fine schedule quotes. Each fee quote joins the 'Description of Violation' cell and the 'Fine' cell of one table row, as printed. The § 10.25.050(3) row has two descriptions (Reserved Parking spaces, and obstructing a city water meter) sharing one $50.00 fine; its quote gives the first description and the fine. Every row of the 2016 schedule is recorded, plus the 2024 § 10.25.100 fine.

Contest form. Although scanned, the PDF carries fillable fields (12 text fields and 5 check boxes, the requester's fields among them), so it is marked fillable. The pages describe handing it in at the Police Department; no online contest is offered.

Prepaying after a summons. Va. Code § 16.1-69.40:1(A) lists violations of § 46.2-1242 'or any parallel local ordinances' (the disability-space rule) among the infractions that can be prepaid, so a summons under City Code §§ 10.25.070(4) or 10.25.390(15) should be prepayable if that section parallels § 46.2-1242 (the City Code was not read). For other City parking sections, prepayment depends on a parallel state provision or a circuit-court schedule under subsection D, which was not found.

Appeal after prepayment. Va. Code § 16.1-132 allows an appeal 'whether or not such conviction was upon a plea of guilty', and § 16.1-69.40:1(B) treats a prepayment as a waiver of trial and a plea of guilty; that a prepaid parking case can be appealed within the 10 days is an inference from these two sections, not something a Staunton or court page states.

corrections: Quotes: all 96 original quotes were re-checked and confirmed; none needed changing. The 33 state-law quotes are substrings of I.text_of for the cited section (whitespace normalised only), across 11 sections, and each cited subsection (46.2-1225(1)-(3), 46.2-1242(B)(1), 16.1-69.40:1(B) and (D), 16.1-69.48:1(A) and (D), 19.2-354.1(B), 46.2-752(J)) matches the text. The 16 web quotes are word for word in fresh copies fetched on 2026-10-11 with the research User-Agent, with HTML comments stripped: the Internet Archive captures of the Parking Tickets page (2026-09-01, the latest capture) and Paying Taxes & Fees (2026-03-08), and the live vacourts.gov Staunton General District Court and tickets_dc pages. The 47 quotes from the scanned City PDFs (Executive Action No. 2024-08 and all six pages of the 2016 fine schedule) were re-read against independent renders of the archived PDF (2026-05-10 capture) and match word for word, fine amounts included. lexflow's check_quotes reports 36 of 36 code quotes matched and 63 other quotes.

Form f1 (Request for Administrative Review of Parking Citation): 'fillable' was false, but the PDF has an AcroForm with 12 text fields and 5 check boxes, the requester's name, address, ticket, plate, violation and reason fields among them. Set to true, matching how fixtures/forms/forms.json uses 'fillable'; a caveat explains.

s15: 'refuse to renew ... after 30 days' notice' misread Va. Code § 46.2-752(J), which requires the agreement to give notice at least 30 days before the current registration expires, and covers issuing as well as renewing. The tow-or-boot sentence now says it needs an ordinance and applies to vehicles parked on public highways or public grounds with three or more unpaid or unsettled tickets (§ 46.2-1216).

s13: the $35 failure-to-appear cost now carries the statute's exception ('unless, after a hearing requested by such person, good cause is shown'), in both how and fee. 'You can be tried in your absence' had no cited basis; it now rests on Va. Code § 19.2-258.1 (heard in absence, then notified of the finding; judge without a jury), scoped to the case where the violation is a traffic infraction under § 46.2-113. Added the court page's 10:30 a.m. trials and contested cases docket and that the page does not mention parking cases.

s14: 'even after ... prepayment' now explains that a prepayment is entered as a waiver of trial and a plea of guilty (§ 16.1-69.40:1(B)), which § 16.1-132 covers; added the jury right on a traffic infraction appeal (§§ 16.1-136, 19.2-258.1). A caveat marks the prepaid-appeal point as an inference.

s11: the draft said to pay 'the City Treasurer' after a denial; the Parking Tickets page says only that you have 15 days from the letter to pay. Reworded to point to the City's stated ways to pay unless the letter says otherwise.

s12: the advice to ask the Police Department or Treasurer to send the contest to court is now marked as a suggestion the City does not describe, and is tied to § 46.2-1225, under which the official who collects uncontested payments certifies contests to the district court.

s10: the follow-up call is now marked as a suggestion the pages do not describe, and the step says no time for the decision is given. s9: added that the Police page gives 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. for in-person crash-report requests, beside the department's 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. business hours. s8: added from tickets_dc that a mailed prepayment counts only on receipt by the court. s5: added that the pages do not say whether the postmark or the date received counts.

Added three state-law legal-basis entries, each checked against I.text_of: § 19.2-258.1 x2 (trial in absence; jury on appeal) and § 16.1-69.40:1(A) (violations of § 46.2-1242 or parallel local ordinances are prepayable), a source row for § 19.2-258.1 (index row 5850), and five caveats (Code Publishing access, how the fine-table quotes are built, the fillable contest form, prepaying a disability-space summons, appeal after prepayment).

Confirmed without change: the full fine schedule (all 42 rows of the 2016 schedule plus the 2024 § 10.25.100 fine are recorded, amounts as printed); the 10-day, 10-business-day and 15-day periods, the $10 late fee and the summons hand-off; the drop-box locations and the check-or-money-order rule for the Central Avenue box; the PO Box 474 address; office addresses, hours and lines for the Treasurer, Police Department, Commonwealth's Attorney, General District Court and Circuit Court; the online-payment rules (Mark for Payment, 3:30 p.m., 4% card fee). Category transportation_parking is the value lexflow/publish/lexipedia.py labels. Privacy: no staff names; the only mailbox is the role mailbox PoliceRecords@ci.staunton.va.us published on the Police page.
open_issues: City Code text was not read: eCode360 and the old Code Publishing site both answered the research client with a Cloudflare challenge on 2026-10-11 and were not attempted. The subject of § 10.25.100, the notice provisions of § 10.05.090, § 10.25.080, and any City Code basis for the late fee, the 15-day period or the Commonwealth's Attorney review remain unconfirmed; the steps rest on the City's Parking Tickets page.

www.ci.staunton.va.us still returns HTTP 403 to the research User-Agent, so every City page and PDF was read from Internet Archive captures (Parking Tickets 2026-09-01, the latest capture); the live pages were not seen.

No source says how someone whose contest is denied can get a court hearing without letting the ticket go unpaid to a summons, gives a deadline for filing a contest, or says whether a contest filed after the 10 days avoids the $10 late fee.

Not confirmed whether a Staunton parking violation is a traffic infraction (so § 16.1-132 appeal, § 19.2-258.1 trial rules and the $51 fixed fee apply) or a civil matter (appeal under § 16.1-106); the contest form speaks of a 'Criminal Summons'. Court costs in a Staunton parking case and whether summonses other than disability-space ones can be prepaid were not found.

Not confirmed whether the Treasurer has a DMV registration-hold agreement (§ 46.2-752(J)) or the City has a tow-or-boot ordinance (§ 46.2-1216); which payment methods the Treasurer's counter takes for parking tickets; and when the schedule's $1.00 courtesy, uncontested and administrative-charge meter amounts apply.
